newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank direct banking goes on-line.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank direct banking goes on-line.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland Plc, one of Britain's leading operators of telephone banking services, on Tuesday detailed its planned launch of an Internet-based direct banking by PC service, to be rolled out this spring.
The bank said in a statement that its product would be Britain's "first fully-fledged, on-line banking service over the Internet".

Initally offered to all its 500,000 telephone banking customers, the PC service will be automatically linked to the phone service and offer a similar range of real-time facilities as well as access to historical account details for six months.

"Currently 11 percent of UK adults use the Internet and we believe that over time the Internet will play an increasingly important role in the lives of many of our customers," retail banking managing director Tony Schofield said.
"It is estimated that 80 percent of European banks will provide a full banking service over the Internet within three years," he added.

The bank stressed the security features of its system and noted, in particular, that access would only be allowed to PCs with a specific registration code that had been recorded and was recognised in a secure format by the system's server computer.

"The bank's confidence is such that...if the customer has taken care to keep their security details secret, the customer will not be liable for any transaction on the account which the customer has not authorised," Royal Bank added.

To be able to hook up to the new service, customers will need a personal computer with a 486 processor as a minimum with either Microsoft Windows 95 or Windows NT software, as well as Internet access.
Users will pay a 1.50 pound ($2.49) monthly charge after an initial free period of six months. ($1=.6021 Pound)
